text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on December 16 in history.
1485 - Catherine of Aragon, first wife of King Henry VIII of England, born. Henry divorced her without Papal approval, starting the English Reformation.

1653 - Oliver Cromwell, leader of the Parliamentary side in the English civil war, declared Lord Protector of England. He went on to establish religious tolerance and allied England with France against Spain.

1742 - Gebhard Lebrecht von Blucher, Prussian Field Marshal, born. In 1815 "Marshal Forward" was defeated by Napoleon at Ligny but played a crucial role in British commander Wellington's victory over the French at Waterloo.

1773 - The Boston Tea Party took place off Griffin's Wharf, a protest against colonists' taxation in Massachusetts. East India tea chests were thrown into the harbour by Bostonians disguised as Indians, prompting British retaliation in 1774, including the shutting of Boston port.

1775 - British novelist, Jane Austen, born. She described her raw material as three or four families in a country village. She was famous for "Sense and Sensibilty", "Pride and Prejudice", "Mansfield Park", "Emma", "Northanger Abbey" and "Persuasion."
1835 - A huge fire spread through New York City, destroying over 600 buildings and causing damage estimated in the region of 20 million dollars.

1838 - The Boers on their Great Trek away from British rule in Cape Colony clashed with Zulu chief Dingaan at the battle of Blood River. The Boers killed 3,000 Zulus. Anniversaries of the battle were important occasions for succeeding generations of nationalist Afrikaners wedded to the policy of "apartheid" or racial separation in South Africa.
1882 - Hungarian composer Zoltan Kodaly born. Among his best known pieces are "Danses of Galanta" and the "Hary Janos" suite.
1920 - One of the worst earthquakes of all time occured in Kansu province, China. Estimated at over 8 points on the Richter scale it killed 180,000 people.
1921 - Camille Saint-Saens, French composer, died. Among his best known works were "Carnaval des Animaux" and "Samson et Dalila".
1944 - Glenn Miller, U.S. dance band leader, disappeared in a light plane over the English Channel. He was best remembered for his "In the Mood" and his signature tune "Moonlight Serenade".

1944 - In World War II, the Battle of the Bulge began when the German forces broke through the allied lines in the rugged Ardennes region, taking U.S. troops by surprise. There were 77,000 Allied and 130,000 German casualties. The German counter-offensive failed.

1945 - Prince Fumimaro Konoe, twice Japanese prime minister, committed suicide rather than face war crimes charges. In the 1920s he worked to curb army powers and prevent an expansion of the war with China. He helped engineer the fall of the Tojo government in 1944 but was suspected of war atrocities.
1949 - Sukarno, Indonesian nationalist, was elected his country's first President after the Netherlands gave up sovereignty. He became president-for-life in 1966; he was replaced by Suharto.
1969 - The British House of Commons voted by 343-185 to approve the permanent abolition of the death penalty.

1971 - Bangladesh, formerly East Bengal and the Sylhet province of Assam in British India, came into existence. Mainly Moslem, the region became an eastern province of Pakistan after India's partition in 1947. Civil war broke out in 1971 and West Pakistani forces in East Pakistan surrendered after India intervened on the side of the secessionists.
1995 - The Israeli army pulled out from Qalqilya, the fourth of six West Bank towns being transferred to Palestinian self- rule by the end of that year under the terms of an Israeli-PLO peace deal.
